snip.t: “What is your immediate airway plan for a patient with a caustic ingestion and a GCS of 8?”
Endotracheal intubation with cuffed tube – airway protection is priority because caustic ingestion can cause rapid airway edema; charcoal and lavage are contraindicated.

| Others | Caustic ingestion, oesophageal cancer (erosion), Barrett's ulcer, severe oesophagitis (infective: CMV, candida, HIV), radiation, and eosinophilic oesophagitis (spontaneous rupture after food impaction) |
